tasks.instruction: Return true when the year is a leap year: divisible by 4 and not by 100, or divisible by 400.
Return the number of set bits in the 32-bit argument.
tasks.note: The top bit was never counted; 33 steps count bit 0 twice.

tasks.instruction: Return the index of the last array element equal to the second argument, or 4 when no element equals it.
tasks.note: The last element was never examined.

tasks.instruction: The function currently tells whether any element of the array is nonzero; change it to return true only when every element is nonzero.
tasks.note: Any-to-all needs both the combining operator and the start value changed.

tasks.instruction: Return the running totals of the array: element k of the result is the wrapping sum of input elements 0 through k.
tasks.note: The third and fourth totals must chain from the previous total.

tasks.instruction: Besides adding 1 to the element at the given index (taken modulo 4), also subtract 1 (wrapping) from the element at the next index, going from the last element round to the first.
tasks.note: The second update must apply to the already-updated array.

tasks.instruction: Split the value into its high 16 bits and low 16 bits, returned as a two-element array with the high half first.
tasks.note: The constants were for bytes, not halves.

tasks.instruction: Return the index of the first element strictly greater than the threshold together with whether one exists (index 4 and false when none); it currently reports the last such element.
tasks.note: Once found, the earliest index must be kept.

tasks.instruction: Return the two arguments as a pair ordered smaller first, larger second.
Return the sum of the whole numbers from the first argument through the second argument, both included (the first is at most the second).
tasks.note: The lower bound must be included: subtract the triangle number of first minus 1.

tasks.instruction: Change the surcharge from 5 percent to 4 percent: return the amount plus the amount divided by 25, rounded down.
tasks.note: Multiplying by 4 before dividing wraps for large amounts.

tasks.instruction: Day numbers count from 0 = Monday in repeating 7-day weeks; return true when the day is a Saturday or Sunday.
Return true when the value has two set bits next to each other.
tasks.note: Neighbouring bits are one position apart.

tasks.instruction: Instead of the plain total, return element 0 minus element 1 plus element 2 minus element 3, with wrapping arithmetic.
Change the mixing step to shift right by 15 instead of 16 and to multiply by 739982445 instead of 73244475.
Return the sum of the decimal digits of the argument; it must handle every 32-bit value, including ten-digit ones.
tasks.note: Ten-digit values lost their leading digit.
